description: We are Team NobhoJol, a multidisciplinary team combining AI, software engineering, data visualization, fisheries biology, aquatic environmental science, and creative design. We aim to use NASA Earth observation and open data to develop science-driven solutions for sustainable fisheries and aquatic ecosystems. We welcome members skilled in GIS, remote sensing, AI/ML, data science, environmental modeling, UI/UX, and scientific communication.
summary:
NobhoAqua is a data-driven web application developed by Team NobhoJol for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.” The platform transforms NASA Earth-observation data into actionable insights for sustainable coastal fisheries and aquaculture in Bangladesh.

By integrating MODIS-Aqua Sea Surface Temperature, Chlorophyll-a, Landsat 8/9 TIRS, and NASA POWER data, our machine-learning pipeline analyzes 119 ocean grid points across the Sundarbans Estuary, Meghna River Mouth, and Kuakata Offshore. Combining a Habitat Suitability Index (HSI) with Random Forest models, NobhoAqua identifies Potential Fishing Zones, predicts habitat suitability for 200 marine species, and provides 24–48-hour harmful algal bloom risk forecasts.

The platform features an interactive ocean map displaying key environmental conditions, species suitability, and potential fishing areas. Our HSI model achieved a reported MSE of 0.0031, while the algal-bloom classifier achieved 79.17% accuracy.

NobhoAqua bridges the gap between satellite data and practical fisheries decision-making, helping fishers and researchers reduce uncertainty, improve resource management, and promote sustainable marine ecosystems, supporting SDG 14 and contributing to SDGs 2, 6, and 13.
details:
NobhoAqua is an innovative, data-driven web application developed by Team NobhoJol to address the challenge “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.” Our goal is to transform satellite-based Earth-observation data into practical intelligence that supports sustainable coastal fisheries, aquaculture, and aquatic ecosystem management in Bangladesh.

How It Works

NobhoAqua integrates open Earth-observation datasets from NASA and USGS, including MODIS-Aqua Sea Surface Temperature (SST), NASA Ocean Color Chlorophyll-a, Landsat 8/9 optical and thermal imagery, and NASA POWER environmental data. These datasets are collected, processed, and analyzed using Python in Google Colab. Our pipeline prepares environmental features across 119 grid points covering three important marine regions: the Sundarbans Estuary, Meghna River Mouth, and Kuakata Offshore.

The platform combines a Habitat Suitability Index (HSI), Random Forest machine-learning models, and species-specific environmental tolerance ranges to generate useful predictions. Its major features include:

  • Ocean Heatmap & Potential Fishing Zones: An interactive map that visualizes ocean temperature, chlorophyll-a, fishing zones, and algal-bloom alerts across the study areas.
  • Species Habitat Suitability Predictor: Allows users to explore 200 saltwater species, examine their environmental requirements, and identify locations with suitable habitats. Hilsa, Tuna, and Shrimp are supported by machine-learning-based suitability predictions.
  • Aquaculture & Harmful Algal Bloom Monitor: Identifies critical, moderate, and normal risk levels and provides 24–48-hour algal-bloom predictions with relevant farm-management advice.
  • Environmental Insights: Presents ocean conditions, suitability scores, species information, and analytical visualizations through an accessible web interface.

Our HSI prediction model achieved a reported Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.0031, while the Random Forest algal-bloom classifier achieved 79.17% accuracy.

Tools and Technologies

We developed the platform using a combination of modern web technologies, data-science frameworks, and AI-assisted development tools.

  • Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, Three.js, and Framer Motion.
  • Backend and Database: Node.js, Express.js, MongoDB Atlas, and Mongoose.
  • Data Science and Machine Learning: Python, Google Colab, Pandas, and Scikit-learn.
  • NASA and USGS Data Sources: NASA PO.DAAC, NASA Ocean Color, NASA Earthdata, NASA GIBS, NASA POWER API, and USGS EarthExplorer.
  • Development and Deployment: Git, GitHub, and Vercel.
  • AI-Assisted Development: ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, and Microsoft Copilot.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of NobhoAqua lies in bringing satellite-based ocean observation, marine ecological knowledge, and machine learning together in one practical decision-support platform. Instead of presenting complex scientific datasets separately, we transform multiple environmental parameters into understandable maps, habitat suitability scores, species recommendations, and early-warning information.

Another innovative aspect is the integration of a 200-species habitat exploration system with Potential Fishing Zone identification and harmful algal-bloom monitoring. This connects marine biodiversity information with practical fisheries and aquaculture needs. We also designed the platform with interactive maps, species-specific 3D visualizations, analytical charts, and learning resources to make scientific information more engaging and accessible.

Benefits and Intended Impact

NobhoAqua is designed for small-scale fishers, aquaculture farmers, fisheries researchers, marine ecologists, and environmental stakeholders. By helping users identify potentially productive fishing areas and monitor environmental risks, the platform aims to reduce blind searching, save time and operational resources, support informed fishing decisions, and improve aquaculture risk awareness.

Our primary focus is SDG 14 – Life Below Water, with additional contributions to SDG 2 – Zero Hunger, SDG 6 – Clean Water and Sanitation, and SDG 13 – Climate Action.

Factors Considered

During development, our team considered Bangladesh's riverine geography, coastal livelihoods, marine biodiversity, environmental variability, data availability, prediction reliability, and accessibility for users with limited technical knowledge or low-bandwidth internet connections. We also considered the limitations of static satellite datasets and machine-learning predictions. Therefore, NobhoAqua is designed as a decision-support tool rather than a guarantee of fishing success or environmental outcomes.

Our long-term vision is to expand the platform with live NASA data integration, Bangla-language support, seasonal species migration information, and advanced aquaculture research capabilities. Ultimately, NobhoAqua aims to bridge the gap between space-based scientific data and real-world aquatic resource management, contributing to a more sustainable future for life below water and coastal communities.

Live Web Application: nobho-aqua.vercel.app
